Just spoke to the Head of AI at a huge company. 

The #1 thing they're struggling with is... what do I do with the AI laggards at our company? 

Like most companies, they’ve found that a Super Pareto Principle is true within their org. 10% of their employees are responsible for 90% of the uplift in productivity/token usage from software engineering to non-technical knowledge work. 

They’ve spent a lot of time & resources on AI enablement from LLM foundations to function-specific trainings and skill building. And yet, the power law of productivity increases hasn’t budged. 

So now they’re left with a few sobering thoughts and hard questions:
1) 90% of people are overpaid and 10% are underpaid 
2) We’d be better off allocating tokens proportionally to the power law, but how do we do that without killing culture? 
3) Significant layoffs are likely warranted and wouldn’t impact overall output, but cultural backlash is a big concern? 
4) How do we hire more power law people as a non technology company? 
5) Is all of our efforts on training and enablement ACTUALLY worth it? 
6) How do we not experience a brain drain where the top 10% all leave because they want to be surrounded by other AI-native 10x’ers?

hits.name: Alex Lieberman
hits.hook: Experian, a $35 billion business with roots dating back to 1826, is surprisingly AI-native.
hits.original_en:
Experian, a $35 billion business with roots dating back to 1826, is surprisingly AI-native.

Its new Chief AI Officer, Vijay Mehta, broke down the credit bureau’s end-to-end AI strategy. 

Complete list of notes...

Big takeaways: 
• Experian is well past proof of concept, with AI capabilities running in production throughout the company. 
• The next stage is what Mehta calls "reimagination." Redesigning how work gets done through delegation to agents vs. prompting chat bots.  
• Adoption is close to universal. 85% of employees actively use the company's AI tools, 88% of developers use coding assistants, and employees built more than 6,000 custom GPTs by the first half of fiscal 2026. 
• They're seeing real ROI. It's measured in time savings, time to value, quality, velocity and traditional before and after financial metrics, not in adoption or token use.

How they built the foundation: 
• Within months of ChatGPT's launch, they trained thousands of employees and put AI policies and guardrails in place. 
• AI traffic was routed through a control plane that gives them observability, monitoring and security. 
• They wrote a GenAI risk framework and built the Experian GenAI Platform, an internal system that lets employees build internal-facing & and customer-facing apps, while accessing company data securely. 
• They rolled out a coding assistant to their large developer base and built their own Experian GPT into products like a digital financial assistant and their Ascend platform. 
• They created a GenAI Center of Expertise, which now sits under Mehta's AI office. 
• Since then, AI has spread across software development, analytics and business operations.

AI inside the employee experience: 
• MyCareer platform recommends learning and career moves and helps managers spot skills gaps. 
• Nadia, an internal AI coach, helps employees set goals, build development plans and prepare for performance reviews. 
• Nadia also gives leaders personalized coaching and 360-degree feedback.

On models and cost: 
• "Not everybody needs the most advanced frontier model. Most workloads can be done with a free or very low-cost model." 
• He compares reaching for a frontier model by default to using a sledgehammer on a job that needs a much smaller tool. 
• They run a mix of open-weight models adapted to their own environment and frontier models accessed through AWS Bedrock. 
• The control plane routes each workload to a model based on the task, language, region and regulatory requirements.

On agent safety: 
• Guardrails are designed into the architecture from the beginning instead of being added later. 
• Their Agent Operating System runs on that control plane, so it can sandbox, monitor and stop an agent process when necessary. "The ability to kill a process, the ability to kill a process, I will repeat that, we've got all of that built in." 
• Their risk profile differs from the frontier labs' because their systems work over a defined body of financial and identity data, without broad access to the internet. "We start with our corpus of data and we put controls around that. And we know exactly how the data is moving."

What the CAIO role actually is: 
• Experian is a big company split into many business units. His job is one common AI strategy and direction: "to make sure that we are all marching in the same direction." 
• He accelerates the AI agenda both internally and externally. 
• Risk, security, compliance and partner choices all come together in the AI office.

AI as the new middleman: 
• Consumers increasingly start their financial journey inside an AI assistant instead of going to Experian or a bank, so Experian is meeting them there. 
• It's the first personal finance app integrated with Google's Gemini. US consumers who connect their Experian accounts can ask Gemini about their FICO credit rating and what's affecting it. 
• Inside ChatGPT it has launched personal loan shopping, credit card shopping and an insurance marketplace. 
• On the enterprise side, ServiceNow is the first integration partner for its Agent Operating System. Under a multiyear partnership, ServiceNow agents tap Experian's Ascend data and decisioning from inside enterprise workflows. 
• It also launched Agent Trust, which verifies that an AI agent is actually connected to the consumer it claims to represent. 
• Could agents eventually skip Experian and get the data somewhere else? He says they can't reproduce it. Decades of longitudinal financial and identity data, plus its provenance and regulatory standing, are what matter when the output drives consequential decisions. "In order to be able to make a decision, you've got to have that trusted data source."

His advice if you're early: 
• Train employees. 
• Set guardrails before deployment. "So much of safety and responsibility comes from the person interacting with the system." 
• Route AI traffic through a controlled gateway where usage can be observed and policies enforced.

Which AI leader should I learn from next?

hits.name: Shruti
hits.hook: 1,200+ pages of the original Chinese Three-Body Problem trilogy, turned into text in a single pass.
hits.original_en:
1,200+ pages of the original Chinese Three-Body Problem trilogy, turned into text in a single pass.

That's what Baidu's newly released Unlimited OCR 2 just accomplished.

Page count isn't the hard part. Any OCR tool can go page by page. The hard part is reading a long document in one pass while keeping track of relevant information from earlier pages, so a table that runs onto the next page or numbering set hundreds of pages back stays consistent. That's where AI document parsers usually degrade.

In Baidu's report, MiniMax-M3 fails past about 223 pages, and Gemini 3.1 Pro and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next lose accuracy as documents get longer. Unlimited OCR 2 stays relatively stable. On MarathonDocBench, built from documents hundreds of pages long, it scored 77.1. The next best model in the comparison scored 33.7.

The trick is Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA). It works like a person transcribing a book: eyes on the current page, looking back at the most relevant earlier pages. So the cost of each decoding step barely grows with length. At 100 pages it was 7× faster per step than full attention.

The first version already has 10M+ downloads on Hugging Face and 28K stars on GitHub.

What I still want to see: independent runs on messy scans, handwriting and mixed-language PDFs. These numbers come from Baidu's report, and a printed novel is a clean source.

If it holds up, contracts, filings and data rooms could be processed in a single run instead of having to be split into separate documents.

hits.hook: Turn any photo into a minimalist Japanese manga print poster with GPT Image 2.5.
hits.original_en:
Turn any photo into a minimalist Japanese manga print poster with GPT Image 2.5. 

Prompt: Task: Create a 3:4 Split-Panel Photo-to-Japanese Illustration Poster

Transform the uploaded photograph into a vertically composed 3:4 comparison poster. The upper half displays the original photograph, while the lower half features a Japanese hand-drawn manga illustration with a limited-color print-poster aesthetic, faithfully redrawn from the same photograph.

Divide the canvas into two equal horizontal sections, each occupying exactly 50% of the total height. Both sections must have the same width. The horizontal division should connect seamlessly, with no gap, border, overlap, or decorative separator.

1. Upper Half — Original Photograph

- Preserve the original photograph exactly as it is.
- Do not redraw, recolor, retouch, or add any text to the photograph.
- Scale proportionally without stretching or distorting the image.
- If necessary, crop peripheral background areas first while preserving the main subject and important visual details.
- If the aspect ratio cannot be accommodated without compromising essential content, extend the edges with a light grayish-cream background. Never invent or reconstruct missing parts of the original photograph.

2. Lower Half — Japanese Hand-Drawn Illustration

Redraw the photograph as a Japanese-inspired hand-drawn manga illustration with a minimalist, limited-color screen-print poster aesthetic.

The original photograph is the exclusive source of the subject's identity, appearance, pose, structure, composition, layout, and relationships between objects.

For people:

- Preserve recognizable facial shape, hairstyle silhouette, expression, pose, gestures, and clothing category.
- Simplify the face into clean manga-style shapes.
- Render hair as grouped, flowing masses rather than individual strands.
- Express clothing through elegant, simplified fashion silhouettes.

For animals:

- Preserve the species, body proportions, distinctive coat-color patterns, and pose.
- Use simplified contours and flat color blocks to retain recognizability.

For objects:

- Preserve the original silhouette, essential structural details, and proportions.

For landscapes and scenery:

- Preserve the terrain, architecture, distribution of visible elements, and spatial depth.
- Redraw the main landscape as a cohesive illustration rather than reducing it to an isolated object.

Preserve all visible contact, overlap, and occlusion relationships. Depict only what is visible in the source photograph. Do not introduce new subjects, props, gestures, or structures outside the original image.

If an additional style reference is provided, use it only for drawing technique, color palette, and layout. Never copy its subjects or content.

3. Linework and Color Treatment

Use a consistent combination of delicate ink outlines, naturally simplified shapes, and limited-color flat fills.

- Ink outline: Near-black "#02030B", with varied pressure, subtle line-weight changes, occasional pauses, and slightly irregular hand-drawn edges.
- Keep internal lines minimal, retaining only the structural details necessary to define form.
- Use clean, continuous, opaque color blocks.
- Merge shadows into a small number of hard-edged color shapes.
- Avoid individual hair strands, dense hatching, photorealistic textures, and excessive decorative detail.
- Preserve the subject's essential natural colors and distinctive identifying color patterns.

Lower-panel background: Light grayish cream "#ECEDE5".

Primary accent: Warm red "#E9444B".

Secondary accent: Muted blue-gray "#5296BD".

Use red as the dominant accent and blue sparingly. Ensure that accent colors complement the subject without compromising its recognizability.

Simplify the background to the cream paper tone, retaining only the environmental details needed to communicate the setting, explain the action, and preserve spatial relationships. For landscape photographs, translate the principal scenery into the illustration rather than omitting it.

4. Lower Panel — Minimalist Poster Layout

Create a refined editorial composition with a small illustration surrounded by generous negative space.

- Treat the subject and essential environmental elements as one cohesive illustration.
- Scale the complete illustration proportionally and center it within the lower panel.
- Keep the entire illustration group within approximately 65–70% of the panel width and 60–65% of the panel height.
- Fit the illustration within these limits without stretching or distorting it.
- Maintain generous light grayish-cream margins on all sides.
- Do not let the illustration touch the edges or fill the entire panel.
- Do not use large background color blocks to fill the empty space.
- Do not add a border around the illustration.

The overall layout should resemble a thoughtfully designed Japanese art-print poster: restrained, balanced, airy, and visually sophisticated.

5. Handwritten Typography

Add two small handwritten text elements within the negative space of the lower panel.

Top area: Place a small, delicate, near-black handwritten phrase, such as:

“FROM LIFE TO LINES.”

Beside the illustration: Add an even smaller, casual handwritten phrase, such as:

“another way to see.”

Generate both phrases automatically based on the subject, setting, and emotional atmosphere of the original photograph. The wording should feel concise, natural, poetic, and contextually relevant.

The example phrases are references for tone and placement only. Do not use them automatically if a more fitting caption can be generated.

Typography must remain subtle and secondary to the illustration. Use a natural handwritten style with fine, slightly imperfect strokes. Ensure all generated text is spelled correctly and legible.

6. Final Output Requirements

- Aspect ratio: 3:4 portrait.
- Upper half: 50% of canvas height, displaying the untouched original photograph.
- Lower half: 50% of canvas height, displaying the Japanese-inspired hand-drawn illustration.
- Equal panel widths, seamless horizontal transition, no gap, no frame, and no overlap.
- Consistent minimalist Japanese manga linework and limited-color print-poster styling.
- Small, centered illustration with generous cream-colored negative space.
- Subtle, context-aware handwritten typography in the lower panel.

Core principle: The original photograph determines what is depicted. The illustration style determines how the lower half is redrawn. Preserve the source's identity and composition while transforming the lower panel into an elegant, minimalist Japanese illustration poster.

My unfiltered thoughts on personal agents.

Grokbot has the best UI and it’s arguably the best overall. In a lot of ways they’re ahead. Their desktop app feels the best, and their multi-bot coordination is great: you can set a team lead and it passes tasks to the other bots. Grokbot also has the best “webhook” feature, which means you can easily turn outside events into triggers that start your agents. That speeds up background workflows like watching your email, Slack and more. It also has Cursor integration, so for bigger tasks Grokbot can spin up a Cursor cloud session with any model (until OpenAI cuts SpaceX off from their models, which I think will happen soon). Unfortunately, running frontier models through Cursor costs more than Claude or Codex. Still, they’re the only ones embracing a team of agents. It’s a really cool idea, but the more bots you have, the more time you spend managing and maintaining them. I’m starting to think one bot with different threads/channels is the right answer, which I’ll get to with Claude Duet.

dots by OpenAI is rough around the edges right now, but it’s probably the most powerful if you use Codex, which I do. dots can spin up Codex sessions in the cloud or locally on your computer. So if you have coding or video editing workflows that need your local files, this is very useful. Codex computer use is also the best in the world: your dot can spin up a local Codex session that fully controls your computer, as long as it’s on. Their real-time voice is incredible. If you have your email and work tools connected, try this: go on a walk with headphones in, ask the agent to summarize your emails, have it draft replies and read them back to you, then send them off. If I remember right, this is close to a workflow you (Tim) used to have with your VAs before AI. It’s my favorite use case for personal agents. The one downside is that you have to call your agent, and it’s an awful experience. It literally rings, and it’s annoying.

Muse by Meta is a toy. I’ve talked to a bunch of finance people I play poker with who all tried it and set up automations, and they all said it doesn’t reliably do what they want. It’s fast, and its user numbers will probably keep growing. But it’s basically free: you get a TON of usage without paying a dime. That’s NOT a trade I’m willing to make. An agent doing high-leverage tasks should be running at the Opus 5.5 or GPT 6.1 Sol level.

Claude Duet - is in early access, so unfortunately not everyone can use it yet. First things first, it runs on Opus 5.5, the best model in the world. I’ve only had access for 72 hours, but Duet feels different from the others. It’s not a personified agent like Grokbot, dot or Muse, which gives it a more professional vibe that I like. When you ask your Duet agent to do something, it spins up a task, which is a new chat thread. All your threads show up in a Tasks tab, so it’s easy to see everything Duet is working on or has finished. And instead of creating more agents (like Grokbot), you create channels, just like Slack (I can tell @anthropic is Slack-pilled). I have a content channel, a finances channel, etc., which keeps different kinds of tasks separate. The only other app I’ve seen do this is Buzz by @jack, and it’s a good experience. Their strong point is documents (artifacts). If you want decks, high-quality docs or design mockups, Opus just wins. Period. It’s not close right now. Their weak point is real-time voice. It’s the worst of the bunch and borderline unusable, though I think they only added it a few days ago.

Instinct lives in iMessage, has no app, and doesn’t do anything notable besides show you product suggestions you didn’t ask for. (Not ads, according to their team.)

My hot take: 
The VM is overrated. SpaceX, OpenAI and Meta all talk about the VM your agent can use and feature it in their marketing. It’s not as useful as you’d think, because more and more websites block bots that visit their site on the cloud VM. All of these companies promise their agents can make payments, but most payments either take forever or get blocked altogether. SpaceX has a cool workaround with Grokbot that routes traffic through your computer so it uses your IP address. But I’d much rather the agent just USE my computer for the task, like dot does by handing it off to Codex. Also, i don't think normal people care about the virtual computer. If anything they get offended they have to "stream a computer". 

The problem with personal agents: by the time you read this, pick one, and test it for 7 days, every one of them will have released 10 new features and the whole landscape will have changed. It’s nearly impossible to keep up.

hits.original_en:
Experian, a $35 billion business with roots dating back to 1826, is surprisingly AI-native.

Its new Chief AI Officer, Vijay Mehta, broke down the credit bureau’s end-to-end AI strategy. 

Complete list of notes...

Big takeaways: 
• Experian is well past proof of concept, with AI capabilities running in production throughout the company. 
• The next stage is what Mehta calls "reimagination." Redesigning how work gets done through delegation to agents vs. prompting chat bots.  
• Adoption is close to universal. 85% of employees actively use the company's AI tools, 88% of developers use coding assistants, and employees built more than 6,000 custom GPTs by the first half of fiscal 2026. 
• They're seeing real ROI. It's measured in time savings, time to value, quality, velocity and traditional before and after financial metrics, not in adoption or token use.

How they built the foundation: 
• Within months of ChatGPT's launch, they trained thousands of employees and put AI policies and guardrails in place. 
• AI traffic was routed through a control plane that gives them observability, monitoring and security. 
• They wrote a GenAI risk framework and built the Experian GenAI Platform, an internal system that lets employees build internal-facing & and customer-facing apps, while accessing company data securely. 
• They rolled out a coding assistant to their large developer base and built their own Experian GPT into products like a digital financial assistant and their Ascend platform. 
• They created a GenAI Center of Expertise, which now sits under Mehta's AI office. 
• Since then, AI has spread across software development, analytics and business operations.

AI inside the employee experience: 
• MyCareer platform recommends learning and career moves and helps managers spot skills gaps. 
• Nadia, an internal AI coach, helps employees set goals, build development plans and prepare for performance reviews. 
• Nadia also gives leaders personalized coaching and 360-degree feedback.

On models and cost: 
• "Not everybody needs the most advanced frontier model. Most workloads can be done with a free or very low-cost model." 
• He compares reaching for a frontier model by default to using a sledgehammer on a job that needs a much smaller tool. 
• They run a mix of open-weight models adapted to their own environment and frontier models accessed through AWS Bedrock. 
• The control plane routes each workload to a model based on the task, language, region and regulatory requirements.

On agent safety: 
• Guardrails are designed into the architecture from the beginning instead of being added later. 
• Their Agent Operating System runs on that control plane, so it can sandbox, monitor and stop an agent process when necessary. "The ability to kill a process, the ability to kill a process, I will repeat that, we've got all of that built in." 
• Their risk profile differs from the frontier labs' because their systems work over a defined body of financial and identity data, without broad access to the internet. "We start with our corpus of data and we put controls around that. And we know exactly how the data is moving."

What the CAIO role actually is: 
• Experian is a big company split into many business units. His job is one common AI strategy and direction: "to make sure that we are all marching in the same direction." 
• He accelerates the AI agenda both internally and externally. 
• Risk, security, compliance and partner choices all come together in the AI office.

AI as the new middleman: 
• Consumers increasingly start their financial journey inside an AI assistant instead of going to Experian or a bank, so Experian is meeting them there. 
• It's the first personal finance app integrated with Google's Gemini. US consumers who connect their Experian accounts can ask Gemini about their FICO credit rating and what's affecting it. 
• Inside ChatGPT it has launched personal loan shopping, credit card shopping and an insurance marketplace. 
• On the enterprise side, ServiceNow is the first integration partner for its Agent Operating System. Under a multiyear partnership, ServiceNow agents tap Experian's Ascend data and decisioning from inside enterprise workflows. 
• It also launched Agent Trust, which verifies that an AI agent is actually connected to the consumer it claims to represent. 
• Could agents eventually skip Experian and get the data somewhere else? He says they can't reproduce it. Decades of longitudinal financial and identity data, plus its provenance and regulatory standing, are what matter when the output drives consequential decisions. "In order to be able to make a decision, you've got to have that trusted data source."

His advice if you're early: 
• Train employees. 
• Set guardrails before deployment. "So much of safety and responsibility comes from the person interacting with the system." 
• Route AI traffic through a controlled gateway where usage can be observed and policies enforced.

hits.hook: 1,200+ pages of the original Chinese Three-Body Problem trilogy, turned into text in a single pass.
hits.original_en:
1,200+ pages of the original Chinese Three-Body Problem trilogy, turned into text in a single pass.

That's what Baidu's newly released Unlimited OCR 2 just accomplished.

Page count isn't the hard part. Any OCR tool can go page by page. The hard part is reading a long document in one pass while keeping track of relevant information from earlier pages, so a table that runs onto the next page or numbering set hundreds of pages back stays consistent. That's where AI document parsers usually degrade.

In Baidu's report, MiniMax-M3 fails past about 223 pages, and Gemini 3.1 Pro and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next lose accuracy as documents get longer. Unlimited OCR 2 stays relatively stable. On MarathonDocBench, built from documents hundreds of pages long, it scored 77.1. The next best model in the comparison scored 33.7.

The trick is Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA). It works like a person transcribing a book: eyes on the current page, looking back at the most relevant earlier pages. So the cost of each decoding step barely grows with length. At 100 pages it was 7× faster per step than full attention.

The first version already has 10M+ downloads on Hugging Face and 28K stars on GitHub.

What I still want to see: independent runs on messy scans, handwriting and mixed-language PDFs. These numbers come from Baidu's report, and a printed novel is a clean source.

If it holds up, contracts, filings and data rooms could be processed in a single run instead of having to be split into separate documents.

Turn any photo into a minimalist Japanese manga print poster with GPT Image 2.5. 

Prompt: Task: Create a 3:4 Split-Panel Photo-to-Japanese Illustration Poster

Transform the uploaded photograph into a vertically composed 3:4 comparison poster. The upper half displays the original photograph, while the lower half features a Japanese hand-drawn manga illustration with a limited-color print-poster aesthetic, faithfully redrawn from the same photograph.

Divide the canvas into two equal horizontal sections, each occupying exactly 50% of the total height. Both sections must have the same width. The horizontal division should connect seamlessly, with no gap, border, overlap, or decorative separator.

1. Upper Half — Original Photograph

- Preserve the original photograph exactly as it is.
- Do not redraw, recolor, retouch, or add any text to the photograph.
- Scale proportionally without stretching or distorting the image.
- If necessary, crop peripheral background areas first while preserving the main subject and important visual details.
- If the aspect ratio cannot be accommodated without compromising essential content, extend the edges with a light grayish-cream background. Never invent or reconstruct missing parts of the original photograph.

2. Lower Half — Japanese Hand-Drawn Illustration

Redraw the photograph as a Japanese-inspired hand-drawn manga illustration with a minimalist, limited-color screen-print poster aesthetic.

The original photograph is the exclusive source of the subject's identity, appearance, pose, structure, composition, layout, and relationships between objects.

For people:

- Preserve recognizable facial shape, hairstyle silhouette, expression, pose, gestures, and clothing category.
- Simplify the face into clean manga-style shapes.
- Render hair as grouped, flowing masses rather than individual strands.
- Express clothing through elegant, simplified fashion silhouettes.

For animals:

- Preserve the species, body proportions, distinctive coat-color patterns, and pose.
- Use simplified contours and flat color blocks to retain recognizability.

For objects:

- Preserve the original silhouette, essential structural details, and proportions.

For landscapes and scenery:

- Preserve the terrain, architecture, distribution of visible elements, and spatial depth.
- Redraw the main landscape as a cohesive illustration rather than reducing it to an isolated object.

Preserve all visible contact, overlap, and occlusion relationships. Depict only what is visible in the source photograph. Do not introduce new subjects, props, gestures, or structures outside the original image.

If an additional style reference is provided, use it only for drawing technique, color palette, and layout. Never copy its subjects or content.

3. Linework and Color Treatment

Use a consistent combination of delicate ink outlines, naturally simplified shapes, and limited-color flat fills.

- Ink outline: Near-black "#02030B", with varied pressure, subtle line-weight changes, occasional pauses, and slightly irregular hand-drawn edges.
- Keep internal lines minimal, retaining only the structural details necessary to define form.
- Use clean, continuous, opaque color blocks.
- Merge shadows into a small number of hard-edged color shapes.
- Avoid individual hair strands, dense hatching, photorealistic textures, and excessive decorative detail.
- Preserve the subject's essential natural colors and distinctive identifying color patterns.

Lower-panel background: Light grayish cream "#ECEDE5".

Primary accent: Warm red "#E9444B".

Secondary accent: Muted blue-gray "#5296BD".

Use red as the dominant accent and blue sparingly. Ensure that accent colors complement the subject without compromising its recognizability.

Simplify the background to the cream paper tone, retaining only the environmental details needed to communicate the setting, explain the action, and preserve spatial relationships. For landscape photographs, translate the principal scenery into the illustration rather than omitting it.

4. Lower Panel — Minimalist Poster Layout

Create a refined editorial composition with a small illustration surrounded by generous negative space.

- Treat the subject and essential environmental elements as one cohesive illustration.
- Scale the complete illustration proportionally and center it within the lower panel.
- Keep the entire illustration group within approximately 65–70% of the panel width and 60–65% of the panel height.
- Fit the illustration within these limits without stretching or distorting it.
- Maintain generous light grayish-cream margins on all sides.
- Do not let the illustration touch the edges or fill the entire panel.
- Do not use large background color blocks to fill the empty space.
- Do not add a border around the illustration.

The overall layout should resemble a thoughtfully designed Japanese art-print poster: restrained, balanced, airy, and visually sophisticated.

5. Handwritten Typography

Add two small handwritten text elements within the negative space of the lower panel.

Top area: Place a small, delicate, near-black handwritten phrase, such as:

“FROM LIFE TO LINES.”

Beside the illustration: Add an even smaller, casual handwritten phrase, such as:

“another way to see.”

Generate both phrases automatically based on the subject, setting, and emotional atmosphere of the original photograph. The wording should feel concise, natural, poetic, and contextually relevant.

The example phrases are references for tone and placement only. Do not use them automatically if a more fitting caption can be generated.

Typography must remain subtle and secondary to the illustration. Use a natural handwritten style with fine, slightly imperfect strokes. Ensure all generated text is spelled correctly and legible.

6. Final Output Requirements

- Aspect ratio: 3:4 portrait.
- Upper half: 50% of canvas height, displaying the untouched original photograph.
- Lower half: 50% of canvas height, displaying the Japanese-inspired hand-drawn illustration.
- Equal panel widths, seamless horizontal transition, no gap, no frame, and no overlap.
- Consistent minimalist Japanese manga linework and limited-color print-poster styling.
- Small, centered illustration with generous cream-colored negative space.
- Subtle, context-aware handwritten typography in the lower panel.

Core principle: The original photograph determines what is depicted. The illustration style determines how the lower half is redrawn. Preserve the source's identity and composition while transforming the lower panel into an elegant, minimalist Japanese illustration poster.

outsiders.hook: Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, featuring 2 new benchmarks and 3 upgrades. For the first time, the majority of the Index is built on private datasets
outsiders.original_en:
Announcing Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, featuring 2 new benchmarks and 3 upgrades. For the first time, the majority of the Index is built on private datasets

The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is our composite measure of model capabilities across tasks reflecting real-world usage today. v5 is our biggest upgrade since v4 launched in January. With v5, 60% of the Index is now based on evaluations with private test sets or held-out answers.

Alongside Intelligence Index v5, we’re launching the Artificial Analysis Progress Index v1, which tracks model capability over time on one continuous scale.

New to the Intelligence Index:

➤ FrontierCode 2.0: Cognition's newly-launched private benchmark of real-world coding tasks, graded on whether a repository maintainer would merge the agent's change

➤ Terminal-Bench-Science: 70 agentic scientific research tasks, run in a terminal environment

Upgraded:

➤ HLE-Diamond (replacing Humanity's Last Exam): a refined 1,000-question version of Humanity's Last Exam, split evenly between reasoning and knowledge questions

➤ AA-Omniscience v1.1: An updated dataset with saturated and public set questions removed, new questions added, and ambiguous or erroneous questions revised

➤ CritPt v2: a private, 40-question hard subset of CritPt v2, revised by the CritPt authors and run with a code-execution tool

Staying in the Index: AA-Briefcase, AutomationBench-AA, GDP.pdf and Terminal-Bench 4.0

Removed from the Index: GDPval-AA v2.1, SciCode, and AA-LCR v1.1

Key results:

➤ Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 58, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (max, 57) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max, 55): Anthropic and OpenAI hold the top five models. Gemini 4 Argon (high) is next at 50

➤ The open weights gap widens from 3 points to 12: Kimi K3.1 Pro (weights not yet released) is the top open weights model at 46. Among released weights, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) and GLM-5.3 (max) lead at 32 - 26 points behind the leader and below Claude Haiku 5.5 (max, 36)

➤ Cost per task varies by more than 13x among the leading models: of the 10 highest-scoring models shown, GPT-6.1 Terra (max) is the cheapest at $0.96 per Intelligence Index task and Claude Fable 5.1 (max) the most expensive at $13.04
outsiders.draft_en:
how to stop overpaying for a frontier model: read Intelligence Index v5 by price, not rank

the podium is tight: Claude Opus 5.5 (max) 58, GPT-6 Astra (max) 57, GPT-6.1 Sol (max) 55, Gemini 4 Argon (high) 50

the bill is not:

- GPT-6.1 Terra (max) costs $0.96 per task

- that spread is more than 13x between models sitting near each other on the chart

if you want open weights, Kimi K3.1 Pro tops them at 46 but you can't download it yet
